title: Dos & don’ts
slide_intent: Teach reviewers to judge an illustration in context. A graphic can clarify a message, obscure a face or change how a photographed subject is understood.
strategic_value: Frontline AIDS can keep its illustrations expressive while respecting the people and issues depicted.
demonstration: Two aligned rows of five small designs pair accepted and rejected treatments. The captions address hero scale, stickers, overlays, hand-drawn marks and use with data.
practical_value: Compare the treatment with the example in the same column. Check that the message remains readable, faces remain visible and the relationship between graphic and subject is appropriate.

content_islands.name: Review guidance
content_islands.spec: Introduce the interaction of illustration, photography and type in the left text column.

content_islands.name: Matched treatment pairs
content_islands.spec: Align each positive example over a related negative example. Keep the check or cross and the explanatory caption with its own image.
